english_verification.review_scope: Representative opening/history/flavour, native ideas, actual Insyaa placeholders and fixed Wiki identity/engineering passages; not exhaustive task reachability. Native English national-idea names and descriptions were compared by localisation key by the primary. Large source intervals are locator envelopes, not a claim to inspect every intervening line or establish complete runtime reachability.
unresolved: League Wiki is a country infobox without detailed national history. Engineering Cadre page describes later setting development, not completed 1444 technology.
The current English primer also supports the refugee-origin account previously attributed to the Chinese Wiki; no precise formation year is newly established.
Original source displays and scores are retained. Insyaa TODO nodes remain unfinished; dev-diary claims do not override local implementation.
The country Wiki is a stub and the engineering entry supplies later-setting context only, not comprehensive current mechanics.

rationale.campaign_length: The current file contains 80 mission definitions in 20 groups; the Insyaa section includes TODO placeholders.
rationale.colonization: Island supply bases, overseas outposts and Aelantiri routes are important directions; unfinished Insyaa nodes are not counted as implemented gameplay.
rationale.complexity: Phased unlocks, facility counts, invention prerequisites, overseas markets and optional Tianlou events interlock.
rationale.dark_story: Pressed convict crews and optional bombing of Tianlou add darkness, though commerce and technological development remain the principal themes.
rationale.difficulty: Early conflict and demanding late-game infrastructure/technology targets both matter; difficulty was not playtested.
rationale.diplomacy: Relations with Luoyip, salt-road contacts, a Tianlou trade agreement and cross-regional commerce allow diplomatic approaches.
rationale.early_pressure: A damaged fleet, competition for nearby tea forests and stronger neighbours make the opening demanding.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: Balloons, airships, artificer inventions and the skyport network run through the middle and later campaign.
rationale.narrative_density: 80 phased definitions and a large event chain connect port recovery, technological revolution and global routes.
rationale.tall_play: The twin harbours, coast, Skyposts, engineering workshops and navigation facilities provide continuing construction goals.
rationale.trade_economy: Tea, salt, whale oil, maritime trade nodes and Skyposts form the core loop.
rationale.warfare: Competition for tea forests and Tianlou, trade-route defence and anti-piracy action require warfare, but land conquest is not the only loop.

identity.appearance: A seven-province coastal republic in 1444. Country history sets the League of Feiten reform, Gangim culture and High Philosophy; province history establishes Y20's starting territory.
identity.formation_scope: An existing country in 1444, not a formable.

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas and ambition only; optional idea groups and racial/government bonuses are excluded. Conditional alternatives are separate, not stacked. Accepting new ideas on formation depends on the actual event/decision and player choice.

description.text: Feiten commands a vast fleet, far too large for us to completely crew with our own citizens without crippling other industries. Since the founding of the League in the mid 1300s, we have taken to pressing prisoners and criminals to serve on our vessels, working for their freedom and granting us the manpower at sea we so desperately require, even if such employment sometimes backfires.

description.text:
Like our famous balloons, Feiten drifts with the winds of change. We are good to our allies, so long as they benefit us, and cruel to our enemies until it is no longer reasonable to act as such.

Some may call us 'deceitful' or 'untrustworthy', but at the end of the day, it is simply the nature of things - and it helps that we always come out on top.

description.text: The New Year's celebrations in Feiten are legendary across Yanshen and beyond, as our skies fill with the most elegant and beautifully crafted balloons, the wealthy looking out over the Jellyfish Coast and our city from their gondolas. Meanwhile, the lower classes release clouds of paper lanterns to brighten the night sky. Truly a sight to behold.

description.text: Our balloons are not just for festivities and presentations; several smaller crafts accompany our armed forces to scout out their routes with a bird's eye view, greatly increasing the ability of our armies to plan their passage through rough terrain.

description.text: The whaling industry is key to our civilization - whale oil not only burns in the furnaces that take our balloons to the sky, but also brightens our city streets. Instead of using cloth or charcoal torches, glass lanterns hang from streetside poles and burn throughout the evenings, astonishing visitors with their longevity and brilliance.

description.text: The revolt of Ping Shuang and her theft of our fleet taught us an important lesson about piracy and the risks of using press-ganged crews. Nowadays, an entire quarter of the Feiten fleet is made up of Diokzatgun, pirate hunters crewed only with citizens of Feiten, trained extensively in naval combat, and granted impunity in assaulting vessels they have reason to believe may have fallen to brigands and mutiny.

description.text: Our vessels, either on the sea or in the air, are common sights across the world. In every coastal marketplace from Anbenncóst to Ynnsmouth, and even south towards Ormam, our traders carry the seal of our city, projecting our mercantile power a world over.

player_overview.avoid_if: Avoid it if you expect mature airships at the start, dislike wars against stronger neighbours, or require all Insyaa missions to be playable now.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Repair the fleet and trading ports, contest tea and salt markets, develop overseas supplies and Skyposts, then connect engineering administration, gnomish exchange, airship inventions and global trade.
player_overview.overview: Feiten is a merchant republic on the Jellyfish Coast in 1444. Pirates have devastated its fleet, while nearby tea forests, salt routes and Tianlou's markets will not yield willingly. Rebuild ports, protect merchants and organise whaling, then turn whale-oil lanterns into Shuimu balloons, establish artificer workshops and skyports, and eventually develop airships and global routes. Its appeal is building a technological revolution yourself; the price is early warfare and extensive later infrastructure.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy artificer technology, airships, maritime commerce, long narratives and transoceanic expansion.
signature_features: Whaling, whale-oil lanterns, Shuimu balloons, skyports and airships form a visible technological progression.
Begin with ports, tea and the salt road, then extend trade towards Rahen, Sarhal and distant oceans.
Competition with Tianlou can lead to a trade agreement or destructive bombing: commercial ambition is not invariably gentle.
player_overview.tagline: Start with whale-oil paper lanterns and turn a coastal merchant league into an airship trading power.

reasons: A clear technological progression from paper lanterns to airships.
Port management and aerial trade form interlocking loops.
A long mission chain connects Haless and overseas routes into one campaign.
warnings: Early pressure from neighbours and the economy.
Complex late-game skyport and artificer prerequisites.
Some Insyaa missions still contain script placeholders.

positive_indicators: Port protection and anti-piracy operations protect merchants and travellers
Engineering, skyports and trade investment support regional prosperity
Technological exchange with gnomes and visitors from Cannor
Controlling Tianlou can open a trade agreement rather than a bombing route
values.rationale: Port security, industrial construction and knowledge exchange support public prosperity. Native ideas describe extensive use of pressed convict crews, while the Tianlou siege route can cause severe devastation and development losses. A trade agreement is available under different circumstances, so bombing is not mandatory. Trade, colonisation and warfare alone do not determine the value score; concrete coercive means reduce dignity and restraint.
red_flags: National-idea text describes extensive use of pressed convict crews
The Tianlou siege event can cause severe devastation, development losses and temple damage
Commercial monopoly and maritime dominance may override other communities' autonomy
